figures.title: GPU-generation ladder relative to H100
figures.caption_draft: Suite-level time of each engine on each host relative to H100 (host / H100; geometric mean of round medians over the queries timed in every round on both hosts), hosts in GPU-generation order. Within a host, markers run from the smallest to the largest scale factor (lighter to darker), with 95% Welch-type intervals on the log scale (rounds unpaired across hosts). Open markers have fewer queries in the suite estimate than at the other hosts (cells that ran out of memory or are unsupported there). Each host is its own campaign; CPU model, architecture, host memory and driver differ, so a GPU-engine ratio is not a pure GPU-generation effect, and CPU-engine ratios reflect the host CPU.
figures.alt_text: Lines of suite-level time relative to H100 across hosts for each engine and suite.

figures.title: GPU-idle fraction by scale and host
figures.caption_draft: Share of nvidia-smi samples with utilization.gpu below 10% inside measured actions of at least one second, by scale factor, one panel per GPU engine and suite, one line per host (line style and shade by GPU generation; the marker is the engine's). descriptive telemetry; not a pre-registered contrast; no causal claim. Samples come every ~200 ms; actions shorter than 1 s are left out and a scale with no action of at least 1 s has no point. utilization.gpu is the share of the sample period in which a kernel was executing, not SM occupancy. The hosts differ in CPU, memory and driver, so a difference between lines is not attributable to the GPU alone.
figures.alt_text: GPU-idle fraction against scale factor for each GPU engine and suite, one line per host.
